newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas soars on weather, storage demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas soars on weather, storage demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were up more than 10 cents in most markets Wednesday as buyers entered the market early to meet weather-related demand and resume storage injections, industry sources said.
Because of this week's production shut-ins as a result of Tropical Storm Josephine, sources said they were forced to slow the pace of storage injections.

The flurry of demand pushed Gulf Coast gas prices into the high-$2.20s to mid-$2.30s, up 10-20 cents from Tuesday, boosted by hot weather in the western U.S. and anticipated colder temperatures in the Midwest.

As Gulf supplies were needed in the Midwest and Northeast, Permian gas demand strengthened further. Prices in the west Texas basin gained another 10-15 cents to the $2.16-2.21 range as buyers continued to purchase gas on the West Coast.
Similarly at the southern California border, prices jumped about 15 cents to the high-$2.20s to low-$2.30s.
However, forecasts are calling for a respite from the sweltering heat by Thursday on the West Coast, though temperatures are expected to remain above-normal through next week.

Midcontinent buyers were also caught short today, forcing prices into the high-teens to low-$2.20s on most of the pipes. Temperatures were expected to be about five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal in the region on Thursday but then warm up by the weekend.
The swarm of buyers boosted prices at the Chicago city-gate into the $2.60s, up about 30 cents from Tuesday's level.
At the New York city-gate, markets were also forced to pay a stiff premium to Tuesday's levels. Traders reported closing most deals in the low-$2.60s.
